summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded bare IP on install
details: The package ships a stub `index.js` that exports a Proxy returning no-op functions for every property, so consumers importing the scoped name `@ecg-internal/js-react-i18n` do not crash the build. `package.json` declares `scripts.postinstall: "node beacon.cjs"`, and `beacon.cjs` POSTs a JSON payload containing `os.hostname()`, `__dirname`, `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The same beacon is also invoked from `index.js` on `require()`. The scoped `@ecg-internal/*` name has no legitimate i18n functionality — the stub exists only to make the beacon's host-reconnaissance exfil succeed silently against any build that resolves this name from the public registry when a private internal package of the same name is expected.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
